summary: - _b) Admit the capital cost as claimed in the Petition and approve the Additional Capitalisation incurred / projected to be incurred._ - _c) Approve the DOCO for the subject Asset as claimed and allow full tariff as claimed under instant petition._ - _e) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulation 2019 as per para 8.3 above for respective block._ _and pass such other relief as the Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice”_ 5. The hearing in this matter was held on 29.5.2025 and 19.8.2025, and the Order was reserved on 19.8.2025. The Respondent(s) have not filed their replies in the matter despite notice. 6. This order is passed considering the submissions made by the Petitioner vide affidavits dated 5.3.2024 and 26.5.2025. 7. Having heard the representatives of the Petitioner and perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. documents placed on record, it is observed that the Implementation Agreement between the Petitioner and M/s SAPDC was signed on 2.8.2021 and as per Sub Clause No. 4.5 of Clause 4.0 “Tariff and Indemnification” of said implementation agreement, the terms and conditions of the 2019 Tariff Regulations notified by the CERC, is applicable and as per the prevailing Regulations, the Petitioner may file the Petition before CERC for determination of tariff. At a few locations, specifically 25/0 & 26/0, the issues could be resolved only after the pronouncement of judgement by the Hon’ble Court(s). The Petitioner has claimed that the considerable amount of time from November 2021 to August 2022, approximately 273 days, has been spent owing to these RoW issues. 24. The Petitioner has submitted the activity-wise details and reasons for delay in Form-12 in respect of the transmission asset as under: 28. The Petitioner has submitted that the implementation of the transmission line was hampered due to various RoW issues on account of the demand for an exorbitant amount of crop compensation, land compensation, construction of structures/buildings/godowns/brick kiln, etc. and the Right of Way of the line. The Petitioner has submitted the various documents in support of its claim of time overrun. 29. We have considered the submissions and perused the documents placed on record. After perusal, it is observed that the Petitioner had encountered the RoW issues at various locations like 8/0, 8/2, 8/3, 7/0, 9/0, 10/0, 13/0, 14/0, 6/0, 7/1, 8/6–8/7, 9/0, 17/0–2 and 25/0 & 26/0 and since 18.11.2021 had taken up the matter with the concerned administrative and police authorities through multiple correspondence to resolve the Row Issues at the earliest to commission the project within the completion schedule. 30. Further, as submitted by the Petitioner, the RoW issues at the aforementioned locations, except Location No. 25/0 & 26/0, were resolved on 9.5.2022. The RoW issues at Location 25/0 & 26/0 were subsequently resolved pursuant to the judgement passed by Collector -cum-District Magistrate, Sitamarhi, on dated 17.8.2022 in 35. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions. The Petitioner shall be entitled to reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the instant Petition, directly from the beneficiary(ies) on a pro-rata basis in accordance with Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. 73. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. It is observed that as per Sub Clause 4.2 (i) of Clause 4 “Tariff _and Indemnification_ ” of Implementation Agreement 80.
